display: Krishna as the Vrindavan cowherd youth
life_stage: Youthful cowherd in Vraja/Vrindavan during the gopi period; not an infant, adult divine form, or Dwaraka king.

visual_bible.age_and_face: A serene youthful face with calm almond-shaped eyes; clearly youth, never infant-like.
visual_bible.skin: Deep matte blue, rendered as opaque mineral pigment.
visual_bible.costume: Yellow dhoti and muted red-orange shawl.
visual_bible.forehead: A smooth forehead may be bare or carry a small traditional U-shaped namam/tilak; keep the mark modest and clearly U-shaped when present.
visual_bible.crown: One simple low gold band with a single upright peacock feather; never a tall tiered crown.
visual_bible.anatomy: Ordinary youthful human proportions, one face, two attached arms and hands, two legs and feet.
visual_bible.style: Follow the series flat matte South Indian temple mural contract.

captain_selected_details.headwear: A single simple low gold band with one upright peacock feather; no tall tiered crown.
captain_selected_details.reason: The captain selected these details because they match the clearest D066 faces and are easiest to hold consistently across generations.

reuse_rule: Every later dasakam depicting Krishna at this youthful cowherd life stage in Vraja/Vrindavan during the gopi period must pass these four reference images and this text as the prompt anchor. Other life stages, including baby Krishna, an adult divine form, and Krishna as Dwaraka king, use separate entries and define their own period references when first reached.
never: no large, elaborate, or nontraditional forehead mark; any namam/tilak must remain small and traditionally U-shaped
no tall tiered crown; use only one simple low gold band and one upright peacock feather
no infant face or infant proportions
no duplicate physical Krishna in a scene
no glossy skin or metallic gold
no copied pose, framing, scene, or props from an identity reference
